issues.body:
The percentage ratchet is wired correctly now, but the complementary presence ratchet still does not cover this crate. Computed against the head checkout: of the 36 entries in PER_COMMIT_CRATES, 35 have an entry in bench/coverage-presence.json and sparq-jsonld is the sole exception (all 36 have a coverage-floor.json entry). `python3 scripts/coverage-presence.py --check` reports "42 ok / 0 fail" and never mentions sparq-jsonld, because check() iterates the floors recorded in coverage-presence.json rather than scanning crates/ for unregistered crates — so a crate absent from that file is silently un-presence-gated, with no loud failure analogous to --check-shards.

That matters because the two gates catch different regressions. The presence file's own _comment states its purpose: a floor on #[test]/#[tokio::test]/#[rstest] counts plus whether the crate keeps its tests/ dir, to catch "a whole crate losing its tests — which the line-% ratchet can miss". sparq-jsonld has a substantial test body to protect (7 files under crates/sparq-jsonld/tests/, ~3.4k LOC, plus inline src tests and the test=true jsonld_conformance example), and deleting large parts of it can leave line% above 86 while the crate's real assurance drops.

The established convention is to wire both halves together: the direct sibling precedent for a no-features crate, commit 1a5f79c1 (#2302), is titled "test(coverage): register sparq-forms ratchets (sq-ncrhx)" and touches coverage-floor.json and coverage-presence.json in the same commit. Filed as minor rather than a blocker because, unlike round 2, the primary line-coverage ratchet is now genuinely enforced.
issues.fix_hint:
Run `python3 scripts/coverage-presence.py --seed` and commit the resulting bench/coverage-presence.json entry for sparq-jsonld alongside the floor entry, with a short note in the established style (crate + bead id + what was measured), mirroring commit 1a5f79c1's sparq-forms entry. Prefer a small margin below the measured count, as the sibling entries do (e.g. sparq-algos 28 measured -> floor 26), so ordinary test churn does not trip the gate. Then re-run `python3 scripts/coverage-presence.py --check` and confirm it reports 43 ok / 0 fail with a sparq-jsonld line.

If leaving it out is deliberate, say so explicitly in the floor-file note (the crate is percentage-gated only) and file a follow-up bead, so the omission is a recorded decision rather than an accident.
issues.title: sparq-jsonld is now the only per-commit crate missing from the test-presence gate (bench/coverage-presence.json)

issues.body:
The note records the number and the command (`COVERAGE_CRATES=sparq-jsonld scripts/coverage.sh`) but not the fixture state, which materially affects the measurement for this crate specifically.

scripts/coverage.sh fetches only three suites (lines 321-323: fetch-conformance.sh, fetch-inference-suites.sh, sparq-shacl/fetch-shacl-tests.sh). It never invokes scripts/fetch-jsonld-tests.sh or scripts/fetch-jsonld-framing-tests.sh, and /tests/w3c/ is gitignored (.gitignore:29), so a fresh CI shard checkout has no JSON-LD suite. Meanwhile crates/sparq-jsonld/Cargo.toml marks the jsonld_conformance example `test = true`, so its 1196-line driver is built and run under `cargo test -p sparq-jsonld`, and its module docs state that when a suite is absent the runner "prints a SKIP notice and exits 0" (it resolves the suite at ../../tests/w3c/json-ld-api/tests). Under llvm-cov the suite-driven arms of that driver are then uncovered.

Consequence: if the 88.73 seed was taken on a work box where an earlier JSON-LD bead had fetched the pinned suites, the shard-1 job measures a lower number, and the 2-point margin is small relative to a driver of that size. The failure would be loud and pre-merge (shard 1 on this very PR), not silent, which is why this is minor rather than major — but it is cheap to de-risk and cheap to document, and without it the robust re-measure loop cannot re-derive the recorded number from the note alone.
issues.fix_hint:
Confirm the seed in an environment matching the shard job (no tests/w3c/json-ld-api present, i.e. the state coverage.sh itself produces) and record that in the note, e.g. "measured with the pinned JSON-LD suites ABSENT, matching the shard env (coverage.sh fetches only the SPARQL/inference/SHACL suites)". If the number was in fact taken with the suites fetched, re-measure without them and reseed the floor from that value so the gate lane can reproduce it.

Worth stating either way, since the crate is the first per-commit entry whose test-target coverage depends on a suite coverage.sh does not fetch.
issues.title: Seed is not reproducible from the note: coverage.sh never fetches the pinned JSON-LD suites, and the crate's conformance example SKIPs when they are absent

issues.body:
Shards 2 and 3 record every later addition inline: "# shard 2 (was 3; ~336s measured; + sparq-reason-el [EL rbox+hasse] + sparq-reason-ql [QL experimental], sq-qcnn.23)" and "# shard 3 (was 4; ~336s measured; + sparq-engine-serialize [seam 1] + sparq-engine-service [seam A2], sq-6vshe.4)". Shard 1's comment is left as "# shard 1 (was 2; ~336s measured)" even though the diff adds a crate to it, so the provenance of the membership change is not discoverable at the line that changed.

Two secondary effects. The sentence immediately above, "each shard's CRATE SET is byte-identical to before, so every non-engine floor is enforced by the SAME crate group as prior", now reads as false for shard 1 (it was already loosened by the sq-qcnn.23 / sq-6vshe.4 additions, which at least annotated themselves). And the "~336s measured" figure no longer describes shard 1's contents; the block above it explicitly asks that per-shard wall-clock stay balanced, since the slowest shard sets the floor. The runtime effect here looks small — `cargo test -p sparq-jsonld` finishes its suites in well under a second on this box, so the added cost is dominated by the instrumented build rather than test time — which is why this is a nit about documentation drift, not a balance objection.
issues.fix_hint: Annotate the shard-1 comment in the existing style, e.g. "# shard 1 (was 2; ~336s measured; + sparq-jsonld [no features], sq-97cxm)", and if the shard was re-timed after the addition, update the seconds; otherwise note that the figure predates it. Optionally soften the "byte-identical to before" sentence to make clear it describes the sq-piapk renumbering rather than the shard sets as they stand today.
issues.title: Shard 1's comment not annotated with the sparq-jsonld addition, unlike shards 2 and 3, leaving the block's "byte-identical" / "~336s" text stale

verdict.summary:
Round 2's blocker (floor seeded for a crate measured by no CI lane) is genuinely fixed, and I verified the fix by running the guards rather than reading the diff alone. sparq-jsonld is now in PER_COMMIT_CRATES (scripts/coverage.sh:115) and in exactly one shard (shard 1, line 226), so `bash scripts/coverage.sh --check-shards` reports OK with 36 PER_COMMIT_CRATES partitioned disjointly by 3 shards + the dedicated sparq-engine pipeline. The floor is therefore enforced by the same `coverage-gate.py --check-robust` step that every sibling floor uses, making the note's claim that "CI's --check-robust is the ratchet of record" true now. `coverage-gate.py --check-monotonic` passes (no floor lowered or dropped) and the floor file stays valid JSON; the one out-of-order key pair (sparq-engine-service before sparq-engine) is pre-existing on origin/main and untouched here.

The other verifiable claims in the note hold. Arithmetic: 5646/6363 = 88.7317%, floor(88.73) - 2 = 86. "The crate defines no Cargo features" is accurate today (crates/sparq-jsonld/Cargo.toml has no [features] table; the http-loader/html features are documented as future beads), so the added comment's assertion that no measure() `case` arm is needed is correct, matching the sparq-forms precedent. I could not reproduce the 88.73 measurement: cargo-llvm-cov is not installed in this environment.

What remains is lower-severity and does not block. sparq-jsonld is now the ONLY per-commit crate absent from bench/coverage-presence.json (35/36 have entries; the sibling PR #2302 was literally titled "register sparq-forms ratchets" and wired both), so the complementary mass-test-deletion gate does not cover it. The seed's reproducibility is under-documented: coverage.sh fetches only the SPARQL/inference/SHACL fixtures, never scripts/fetch-jsonld-tests.sh, and the crate's `test = true` conformance example SKIPs when tests/w3c/json-ld-api is absent, so the fixture state at seed time changes the numbe… [truncated 89 chars]
